content.content:
=== V4__invoices.sql ===
-- Third domain table: an invoice is an amount that belongs to a project. IDENTITY id so the app
-- generates ids on create, while the test seed inserts explicit ids (GENERATED BY DEFAULT lets a
-- supplied id win). project_id is a FK to projects so an invoice always points at a real project.
-- amount is money, so a fixed-scale DECIMAL (two places) rather than a float.
CREATE TABLE invoices (
    id         BIGINT GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    project_id BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES projects (id),
    amount     DECIMAL(12, 2) NOT NULL
);
=== V5__invoice_status.sql ===
-- Paying an invoice is a status transition, so an invoice now carries a status. New and existing
-- rows start UNPAID (the DEFAULT), and marking one paid flips it to PAID. A short VARCHAR holds the
-- status token the UI shows and the audit record names; NOT NULL + DEFAULT keeps every row valid.
ALTER TABLE invoices ADD COLUMN status VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'UNPAID';
=== V9__invoice_draft_status.sql ===
-- An invoice now moves through a lifecycle: DRAFT -> SENT -> PAID. A freshly raised invoice starts
-- as a DRAFT (it hasn't gone out yet), so the status column's default becomes 'DRAFT'. Additive: an
-- ALTER of the existing column default, no data rewrite — rows carry whatever status they were given.
ALTER TABLE invoices ALTER COLUMN status SET DEFAULT 'DRAFT';
=== V15__invoice_line_items.sql ===
-- An invoice is no longer a single typed-in figure: it is built from LINE ITEMS, each a thing the
-- user is charging for (a description, how many, the price each). The invoice amount is the SUM of
-- every line's quantity times its unit price. This table holds those lines; invoice_id is a FK so a
-- line always belongs to a real invoice. IDENTITY id (GENERATED BY DEFAULT) so the app generates
-- ids on create while the test seed inserts explicit ids.
CREATE TABLE invoice_line_items (
    id          BIGINT GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    invoice_id  BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES invoices (id),
    description VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    quantity    INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (quantity > 0),
    unit_price  DECIMAL(12, 2) NOT NULL CHECK (unit_price >= 0)
);

-- An invoice's amount is now DERIVED from its line items, so a fresh invoice with no lines yet sums
-- to zero (a DRAFT the user hasn't added anything to). The old "amount must be > 0" guard (V6) no
-- longer holds — drop it. The amount column stays as the maintained sum of the invoice's lines.
ALTER TABLE invoices DROP CONSTRAINT invoices_amount_positive;
=== V20__invoice_payments.sql ===
-- What a client has PAID against an invoice: each payment is an amount received on a date. An
-- invoice can be paid in parts, so these are rows (not one figure on the invoice). invoice_id is a
-- FK so a payment always belongs to a real invoice. IDENTITY id (GENERATED BY DEFAULT) so the app
-- generates ids on create while the test seed inserts explicit ids. The amount must be positive (a
-- payment is money received), and the date it was paid is required.
CREATE TABLE invoice_payments (
    id          BIGINT GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    invoice_id  BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES invoices (id),
    amount      DECIMAL(12, 2) NOT NULL CHECK (amount > 0),
    paid_date   DATE NOT NULL
);
=== V3__projects.sql ===
-- Second domain table: a project is a name that belongs to a client. IDENTITY id so the app
-- generates ids on create, while the test seed inserts explicit ids (GENERATED BY DEFAULT lets a
-- supplied id win). client_id is a FK to clients so a project always points at a real client.
CREATE TABLE projects (
    id        BIGINT GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    name      VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    client_id BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES clients (id)
);
=== V1__clients.sql ===
-- First domain table: a client is a name + email. IDENTITY id so the app can generate ids on
-- create, while the test seed inserts explicit ids (GENERATED BY DEFAULT lets a supplied id win).
CREATE TABLE clients (
    id    BIGINT GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    name  VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    email VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL
);

The change is complete and the acceptance test passes. Here's what I implemented as a single additive full-stack change.

## What the request needed
"Work out whether an invoice is paid, part paid or owing, from the payments I've recorded — and stop flipping it to paid by hand." So invoice status is now **derived from payments** rather than a flag someone sets.

## Database
- **`V21__invoice_payments_invoice_index.sql`** — index on `invoice_payments(invoice_id)`, supporting the new per-invoice payment-sum read path the derivation leans on.

## Server (OfficeFloor / Spring)
- **`InvoiceView.ofDerived(...)` + `deriveStatus(...)`** — the rule in one place: `PAID` once payments cover the amount, `PARTIAL` once some is paid, otherwise the invoice's own lifecycle status (`DRAFT`/`SENT`). A zero-amount invoice is never paid off nothing.
- **`ListInvoices`** now injects the payment repo and returns the derived status per row.
